name: Nador
hero_subtitle: Where the Rif meets a vast Mediterranean lagoon: Marchica, a lively corniche, mountain viewpoints and wild headlands toward Cap des Trois Fourches.

info.best_time_val: May – October for beaches; spring & autumn for hiking and views
info.vibe_val: Lagoon, corniche, Rif coast, ferry gateway

overview.title: Welcome to Nador — lagoon light and Rif coast
overview.p1: Nador sits on Morocco’s northeastern Mediterranean shore, defined less by an old town than by water: the Marchica lagoon (Mar Chica), one of the largest saltwater lagoons in the Mediterranean basin, stretches for roughly twenty-five kilometres beside the city.
overview.p2: Evenings belong to the corniche. Day trips pull you toward Mount Gourougou, the dramatic Cap des Trois Fourches peninsula, quieter beaches like Charrana and Ras El Ma, and the working port of Beni Ansar. Melilla lies just across the border for a short passport day if you want the contrast.

places.title: Must-visit places in Nador
places.subtitle: Lagoon, corniche, mountain, headland and nearby beaches.

marchica.title: Marchica Lagoon (Mar Chica)
marchica.desc: A vast Mediterranean lagoon beside the city — calm water, birdlife and the defining landscape of Nador.

corniche.title: Nador Corniche
corniche.desc: The city’s evening waterfront — cafés, lagoon views and the social heart of town.

gourougou.title: Mount Gourougou
gourougou.desc: A low mountain above Nador with trails and wide views over lagoon, coast and Melilla on clear days.

cap_trois_fourches.title: Cap des Trois Fourches
cap_trois_fourches.desc: A dramatic peninsula of cliffs and empty coast — one of Morocco’s wildest Mediterranean landscapes.

charrana.title: Charrana Beach
charrana.desc: A cliff-backed cove of clear water about an hour from town — quieter swimming away from the lagoon strip.

beni_ansar.title: Beni Ansar Port
beni_ansar.desc: Working harbour and ferry terminal — landings, seafood and the practical edge of the city.

kasbah_selouane.title: Kasbah of Selouane
kasbah_selouane.desc: A 17th-century Alaouite fortification inland from Nador — history with a short road hop.

ras_el_ma.title: Ras El Ma (Cap de l’Eau)
ras_el_ma.desc: A calmer coastal town and beach east of Nador — sand, fishing boats and open Mediterranean light.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day plan for Nador
itinerary.subtitle: Lagoon and corniche first, then mountain or headland, then a beach day.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: First look at the lagoon from the corniche and open water edges.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Simple lunch, optional short lagoon walk or rest before evening.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Cafés, lagoon light and seafood when the promenade fills.

eat.title: Where to eat in Nador
eat.subtitle: Fresh fish, lagoon-side tables and simple town plates.

nomad.title: Port-side fish
nomad.desc: Fresh catch near the harbour when boats are in.

jardin.title: Hotel restaurants
jardin.desc: Reliable options if you stay in a larger hotel.

fassia.title: Town café stop
fassia.desc: Coffee and a pause between errands.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: Town and corniche are walkable; beaches and Cap des Trois Fourches need a car or organised transfer.

bargain.title: Sun & seasons
bargain.desc: Mediterranean sun is strong in summer. Spring and autumn are ideal for Gourougou and the Cap.

water.title: Cash & border
water.desc: Carry dirhams for taxis. If you day-trip to Melilla, bring a valid passport and check border hours.

daytrips.title: Best outings from Nador
daytrips.subtitle: Lagoon loops, mountain views and wilder Mediterranean coast.

tiout.title: Cap des Trois Fourches
tiout.desc: Half or full day to cliffs, empty coast and one of the region’s strongest viewpoints.

antiatlas.title: Mount Gourougou
antiatlas.desc: Short hikes and panoramas over Nador, the lagoon and Melilla on clear days.

taliouine.title: Charrana or Ras El Ma
taliouine.desc: Beach day with clearer swimming than the inner lagoon strip.

agadir.title: Melilla (passport day)
agadir.desc: Spanish enclave across the border — modernist streets and a sharp cultural contrast.

q1.question: How many days in Nador?
q1.answer: Three days cover the lagoon, corniche and one mountain or beach outing.

q2.question: Is Nador only the lagoon?
q2.answer: Marchica is the signature landscape, but Gourougou and Cap des Trois Fourches add wild coast.

q3.question: How do I get to Nador?
q3.answer: Flights to NDR, ferries via Beni Ansar, or road links along the northeastern Rif.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: May to October for swimming and corniche evenings.
